signals.title: CAD/JPY — G10 Bilateral Theme + Data Divergence
signals.text: CAD/JPY is the primary G10 expression of outperformance this week as CAD average returns hit +0.951% while JPY lags at -0.917%. The 1.868% spread between the two reflects a major divergence in data momentum, as the CAD ESI at +11.6 contrasts with the broad JPY weakness despite its own positive data index. While USD/JPY holds at 159.04, the CAD/JPY cross at 114.615 benefits from a 125bp carry advantage favoring CAD. The market is rewarding the CAD's resilient data profile against the JPY's persistent inability to capitalize on domestic GDP stability. Trade bias: Long CAD/JPY; strong bilateral G10 theme favors continued CAD outperformance. Catalyst: next BoC meeting (mkt: 100% hold priced) — 9 Sep. Risk: G10 bilateral spread compresses below 1.20% as JPY safe-haven demand revives.

signals.title: EUR/USD — Macro Repricing + Vol Premium
signals.text: EUR/USD trades at 1.1585, clearing the SMA20/50 cluster at 1.1468/1.1478 as weak US retail sales and consumer sentiment reports pressure the dollar. The options market is aggressively pricing protection for further upside, with ATM IV at 7.1% against an HV30 of 4.3%, creating a significant +2.8% vol premium. While CFTC positioning shows Leveraged Funds remain net short EUR by -73,049 contracts, the current macro shift toward fading Fed hike expectations creates an asymmetric short-squeeze risk. The ECB's restrictive real rate of +0.09% now competes more effectively against a USD real rate of +1.52% as nominal Fed expectations peak. Trade bias: Bullish EUR/USD; macro-driven dollar weakness forces a squeeze of stale spec shorts. Catalyst: next ECB meeting (mkt: 90.0% hike priced) — 10 Sep. Risk: EUR/USD close below the SMA20/50 cluster at 1.1470 re-establishes the bearish trend.

signals.title: USD/JPY — Options Skew + Carry Tension
signals.text: USD/JPY at 159.04 remains supported by a 275bp Fed-BoJ carry advantage, yet the options market signals severe caution as the pair stays near the 160.00 intervention watch level. The 25d risk reversal shows a strong -2.08 put skew, indicating that institutional desks are paying a premium for JPY-strength protection despite the carry-positive environment. This options complacency break—where IV at 7.2% sits 1.4 points below realized HV30—suggests the market is underpricing potential tail-risk moves near the 160.00 handle. Leveraged Funds are net short JPY by -63,633 contracts, leaving the pair vulnerable to a rapid unwind if BoJ hike bets continue to intensify as signaled by latest headlines. Trade bias: Neutral/range USD/JPY; carry advantage at 159.04 neutralized by intervention risk and heavy downside options skew. Catalyst: next BoJ meeting (mkt: 50% hike priced) — 18 Sep. Risk: sustained break above 160.00 triggers BoJ verbal or physical intervention.

signals.title: AUD/USD — Positioning Extreme + Retail Divergence
signals.text: AUD/USD trades at 0.7097, holding above its SMA20/50/200 cluster (0.6936–0.7019) as the pair extends its 1W gain of +0.90%. CFTC data shows a crowded spec long with LF net at +37,990 (72.1% long), which typically signals late-cycle trend exhaustion. However, retail sentiment is 78% short, creating a classic institutional-vs-retail divergence where retail traders are unsuccessfully fading the trend. The 60bp AUD carry premium over USD continues to support the bid while the ESI at -10.9 suggests that despite disappointing data, the carry and technical momentum remain dominant. Trade bias: Long AUD/USD; trend supported by carry and retail contrarian flows despite crowded institutional positioning. Catalyst: RBA meeting — 29 Sep. Risk: AUD/USD close below the SMA20 at 0.7019 signals a trend reversal and positioning unwind.
